newsitem.title: USA: NCRA Kansas gasoline making unit hobbled by fire.
newsitem.headline: NCRA Kansas gasoline making unit hobbled by fire.

text.p: National Cooperative Refinery Association (NCRA) said Tuesday a small fire on Monday hobbled the gasoline making unit at its 74,000 barrel-per-day McPherson, Kansas, refinery.
The company said the refinery is still making gasoline but at unspecified reduced rates. The fire Monday morning hit the continuing catalytic cracker reformer, which makes gasoline components.
The refinery has a reforming capacity of 19,800 bpd, according ot published data.
The company could not say when the unit will return to full production, but gasoline traders were predicting a two-week partial downtime.
"We've got a plan for repairs. The refinery is continuing to run but we don't know how long the unit will be down," said a company official.
News of the fire firmed differentials for unleaded gasoline in the Midcontinent markets by a quarter to a half cent on Tuesday.
Group Three unleaded differentials traded at 0.35 cents over August NYMEX futures, while Chicago material was pegged at 0.25/0.50 cents above the print.
